title: Formulas and business rules
intro: Every number O2S works out and every limit it checks: the formula, its unit and rounding, a worked example, where it lives in o2s.html, the ruling it comes from and the test that proves it. The last item lists every limit in one table.

items.title: F-001 · How much a batch may make (the 115% ceiling)

blocks.p: Ceiling (Kg/L) = plan x (1 + 15 / 100). A shift entry is refused when produced so far + this entry > ceiling + 0.001. Only the upper side is limited; a batch that makes less is closed with a variance reason. Past the ceiling, the Plant Manager or COO raises the plan first.

items.title: F-002 · Room left to log on an open batch

blocks.p: Room = round2(ceiling - produced), never below 0. For a PO batch, room = the smaller of that and (PO line ordered - PO line produced). A closed batch, a pool, or a batch with no plan has 0 room. The Log more output button shows floor(room) and only when room >= 1 and the person holds the shift.log right (_logMoreRoom).

items.title: F-003 · A PO batch never makes more than the PO

blocks.p: For a batch made for one PO line: the entry is refused when entry > (ordered - produced on the line) + 0.001.

items.title: F-004 · Yield variance at batch close

blocks.p: Variance (Kg/L) = round2(plan - produced). Above 0.001 the close needs a reason from the variance list and the Plant Manager is notified (varianceNotify). The Plant Manager's Yield short job is raised when the closed batch has variance > 0.5 and he has not marked it seen. Actual yield = produced.

items.title: F-005 · Remainder on a batch, and reconciling it

blocks.p: Remainder = max(0, produced - packed - disposed). Reconcile is saved only when loss + by-product + divert + rework + kept as stock is within 0.5 of the remainder. A loss above 0 needs a loss reason. Disposed rises by (remainder - kept as stock); kept stock stays packable. A second reconcile adds to the first.

items.title: F-006 · Lab-cleared Kg on a batch

blocks.p: Cleared = sum over lots with an approved COA of min(lot qty, certifiedKg, or lot qty when no certified figure). A batch with no lots uses its own COA against produced.

items.title: F-007 · Packable Kg on a batch

blocks.p: Packable = max(0, min(cleared, produced - disposed) - packed). 0 when the batch is reconciled with nothing disposed and no stock kept. Ready to pack also needs an approved lot and the batch not a pool or voided (batchPackNow).
Worked example: produced 2,010, cleared 1,000, packed 300, disposed 0: packable = min(1,000, 2,010) - 300 = 700.

items.title: F-008 · A settled batch (may be closed in bulk)

blocks.p: Settled = open, not a pool, voided or by-product, produced > 0, remainder <= 0.5, and round2(plan - produced) <= 0.001. Only settled batches can be closed in bulk; a batch with a variance never can.

items.title: F-009 · Made so far brought to what was packed (batch for several POs)

blocks.p: For each PO on a multi-PO batch: credit = min(round2(produced x its planned share / total share), line ordered), capped by what the shift log credited, less any earlier true-up. Over = round2(credit - packed for that line from this batch). If over > 0.5, the line's produced falls to max(line packed, produced - over). Runs only when the batch is closed and nothing is left (remainder <= 0.5); never takes the same Kg twice.

Worked example: AP26012 made 1,010; COBO's line was credited 745.39 but only 300 was packed for it. Over = 445.39, so COBO's made so far falls to 300 and What to make asks for 1,700, not 1,255 (code comment).

items.title: F-010 · Packs = Kg / pack size

blocks.p: Packs = round2(Kg packed / pack size). Pack size = the PO line's pack, else the product catalogue's pack. Whole when |packs - round(packs)| < 0.001. The person ticks that the packs match; the tick is tied to Kg and pack size, so changing either clears it. No pack size: the entry saves without packs and no tick.
Worked example: 500 Kg/L at 25 per pack = 20 packs (whole). 510 Kg/L = 20.4 packs, called out as not whole.

items.title: F-011 · A packing entry above the limit is cut, not refused

blocks.p: Kg saved = min(typed, batch packable, PO line ordered - packed). The cut is shown with the packs for the real figure. A divert above what the pool holds is refused instead. The 2 correction screens never cut; their own checks refuse.

items.title: F-012 · Big pack run (over 10,000 Kg/L)

blocks.p: Flag when this entry > 10,000, or when the total of entries on the same date by the same shift and in-charge (this one included) goes over 10,000 with this entry. Saved and counted, never stopped. Only the Production Manager marks it Seen.
Worked example: Morning, in-charge Faisal: entries of 6,000 and 5,000 on 15 Oct. The second takes the shift to 11,000, so only it is flagged. One entry of 10,025 is flagged by itself.

items.title: F-013 · The price on a new order (5% band)

blocks.p: Last price = this customer's latest net price for the product (by PO received date), else the latest to anyone. Diff = (net typed - last) / last. When |diff| > 0.05 a reason of at least 5 characters is required, kept on the line with the last price. Net typed = typed / 1.05 when the order is FED Inclusive. No check for FOC or when no earlier price exists.
Worked example: last price 200: typed 205 needs no reason (+2.5%); 211 needs one (+5.5%); 189 needs one (-5.5%); 210 on an Inclusive order is 200 net, no reason.

items.title: F-014 · FED split on the PO

blocks.p: Exclusive: FED = round2(value x 0.05), total = value + FED. Inclusive: sub-total = round2(value / 1.05), FED = value - sub-total, total = value. None: FED 0.

items.title: F-015 · Net price and what a sale is

blocks.p: Net price = invoice price / 1.05 on an FED Inclusive order, else the invoice price; FOC = 0. A sale = Kg x net price, counted on the day the truck leaves the gate (released or delivered, or an old truck counted in dispatched). Every money figure uses this one rule.

items.title: F-017 · What raw material allows (rmAllows)

blocks.p: rmAllows = ordered when RM is ready, full or received; = canMakeKg when RM is partial; else 0. Production for a line is asked only up to min(ordered, rmAllows).

items.title: F-018 · Base shared by order lines, and the run for the rest (plBaseShare)

blocks.p: Order lines on a base are queued: lines waiting for the client last, then by PO received date, PO and line id; close-short-requested lines take nothing. Each line in turn takes ready = min(need, ready left) and lab = min(need - ready, base with the lab left). Run for the rest = min(rmAllows, ordered) - packed - its ready share - its lab share; a run card shows only when this is > 0.5. Every Pack from base card still shows all the ready base.

Worked example: base ready 3,000, line needs 10,000: Pack from base for 3,000 and a run for 7,000. Same line with raw material for 4,000 only: run for 1,000. Same line with all raw material and 5,000 more at the lab: run for 10,000 - 3,000 - 5,000 = 2,000 (with raw material for 4,000 and 5,000 at the lab there is no run card). 600 ready and 2 lines of 500: the older PO takes 500, the newer 100 and gets a run for 400.

blocks.note: Corrected 16 Oct 2026 (independent check against the code): the lab example read as if it followed the 4,000 raw material case; it holds only with all raw material (rest = min(rmAllows, ordered) - packed - ready - lab).

items.title: F-019 · Base made and with the lab (plBaseLabKg)

blocks.p: For each normal bulk batch of the base (not voided, pool, by-product, consolidated, or reconciled without kept stock): min(sum of lot qty with no result yet, produced - disposed - cleared), never below 0. Summed over batches.

items.title: F-020 · A line's packing clock and 'moving' (plLinePack)

blocks.p: Last pack = the newest pack record (not reversed or void) of the same product on any PO of the same client (cancelled or voided POs and POs with no client left out). Clock start = the latest of last pack, PO received and base first ready. Days = calendar days from the start to today, never below 0. Moving = last pack less than 7 days ago.
Worked example: Enroot for Maxim packed on PO 22868 on 13 Oct: on 15 Oct PO 22867's Enroot line has 2 days, so it is moving, not stuck.

items.title: F-021 · Stuck limits (PL_ constants)

blocks.p: Open batch below plan with no move for 3 days or more: stuck. Open batch at plan with nothing left, or waiting for the lab, with no move for 2 days or more: stuck. An order line with nothing packed for 7 days or more while cleared stock is ready: stuck. Cleared stock with no order waiting: held, flagged amber at 180 days or more.

items.title: F-025 · Production stall days (acProduceStallDays)

blocks.p: Bulk base line: days since the later of the last logged output (shift entry with Kg > 0) on any normal bulk batch of the base and the PO received date. Line with its own PO batch: days since the latest of its lot dates, opened date and production log dates. No batch: days since RM ready, else PR raised. Stalled at 4 days.

items.title: F-026 · Escalation days per job

blocks.p: Escalated when the job's waiting days (actTiming) >= the limit; Open Production uses stall days (F-025). Never escalated: Pack from base or Open Production while the line waits for the client, Open Production while the line is moving (packed in the last 7 days), and a Pack job whose PO lines all wait for the client. Calendar days, plant time. Who is told and the ruling per job: logic tab LG-12.

blocks.note: Confirm delivery's 99 days means the table never fires; delivery has its own ladder (F-030). Lab test escalates to the QCM by the clock (F-027).
Corrected 16 Oct 2026 (independent check against the code): added the exceptions written in acEscalation (waitClient, moving, batchLinesWaiting).

items.title: F-027 · Lab due times and lab late

blocks.p: A v2 test is due its own time after assignment: 30 min sampling + the test time + 30 min reporting (QC manager's Estimated Time For Test Report); the QCM sets the times in hours (0.25 steps). The sample is due when its longest test is due. Late by = now - due (ms), 0 if not past. A late test escalates to the QCM (days shown = floor(late / 1 day)). Lab late reaches the Plant Manager when the sample is still open more than 1 day after its due time.

blocks.note: Corrected 16 Oct 2026 (independent check against the code): labV2Items needs late by more than 86,400,000 ms, so at exactly 31 h there is no Lab late yet.

items.title: F-030 · Delivery confirmation ladder

blocks.p: Days = calendar days from the release (approved) date, else the truck date. Day 0: the dispatcher (gate pass issuer, else loader). Day 1 on: also Supply Chain (not the dispatcher himself if he is in Supply Chain). Day 2 on: also the Plant Manager.
Worked example: released 13 Oct: on 13 Oct only the dispatcher; 14 Oct Saad too; 15 Oct the Plant Manager too.

items.title: F-031 · Waiting for the client: 1 to 30 days

blocks.p: Date must be 1 to 30 days after today (UTC date difference); reason at least 5 characters; the same date again is refused. The line waits through the date and is no longer waiting from the day after. Only Supply Chain or the COO marks or ends it.

items.title: F-032 · Deferring a job: 1 to 30 days
items.ask: A deferred job set to come back on 22 Oct reappears on 23 Oct. Should it: A come back on 22 Oct as the sheet says, B stay as it is and the sheet say 'hidden until', C you want to see it first?

blocks.p: Return date must be after today and no more than 30 days away; 7 days is offered. Reason from a fixed list. The job is hidden while the return date >= today.
Worked example: deferred on 15 Oct until 22 Oct: hidden through 22 Oct, back on 23 Oct.

blocks.note: The sheet says 'Comes back on' the date picked, but the code keeps it hidden on that date too, so it comes back the day after.

blocks.p: Days late = calendar days from the date typed to today (plant time). Late when days late > the allowance; a late entry needs a reason of at least 6 characters (evDateGate) and counts against the department's current number. A date in the future is refused. The COO may change the allowances in master data.

items.title: F-038 · Short close: the gap and the packed check

blocks.p: Gap = max(0, round2(ordered at close - delivered at close)), frozen at the moment of asking. 'We could not supply' and 'Raw material never arrived' are refused when open = ordered - delivered > 0.5 and packed but not delivered >= open - 0.5. A reason marked ours counts against us: We could not supply, Raw material never arrived, Price credit or terms, and Other (an unknown code counts against us too). The 3 customer reasons and Supplied from stock outside O2S do not. Fulfilment (aggOpen) leaves closed lines out on both sides; ordered is never rewritten.

items.title: F-039 · Stock reserved for trucks (reconcileLotShipKgV1)
src: fn ensureState (runs it on every load)

blocks.p: Per order line, packing runs are sorted oldest first (date, then id). A truck planned from 15f (lotExact) reserves its own runs, each capped at that run's QA-passed Kg; any overflow or a run not in the line's pool goes to 'loose'. To spread = max(0, dispatched - Kg of released exact trucks) + Kg on not-yet-released older trucks + loose. Each run's shipKg = its exact Kg + min(to spread left, QA-passed - exact), oldest first.

items.title: F-040 · Duplicate shipment rows self-heal (dedupeShipmentsV1)

blocks.p: For each PO and product, only trucks already counted in dispatched: while the shipment rows add up to more than dispatched + 1, remove the duplicate row (same DC) whose Kg is closest to the excess, at most 50 times. Never below dispatched.
Worked example: dispatched 1,000, rows of 1,000 and 1,000 on the same DC: one row is removed.

items.title: F-041 · Job age colours and urgency on Today

blocks.p: Chip: 0 days green 'new today', 1 to 6 days amber, 7 days or more red. Urgency: waiting for the client 3 (never urgent); overdue order 0; a job with a deadline: due today or past 0, tomorrow 1, in 2 days 2, else 3; otherwise 7+ days 1, 3+ days or a hot order 2, else 3. Sort: urgency, nearest deadline, days overdue, days waiting.

items.title: F-042 · PO tracker: due soon, ageing, stalled

blocks.p: Due soon: not overdue and a line due in 0 to 3 days. Ageing (t2sev warn): 3 days or more in the current stage, and not overdue. Stalled: 7 days or more in the current stage and not overdue. Overdue: committed date on or before today (the code compares the committed date at midnight with the time now, so a line is already overdue on its committed day, 0 days past), not delivered within 0.5 or closed short, and the committed date not before the PO was received.

rows: Math.round for due soon; calendar days for stage age

blocks.p: Worked example: a line committed for 17 Oct, today 15 Oct: due soon (within 3 days). On 17 Oct itself it is overdue.

blocks.note: isStalled and t2sev are not pinned by a test.

Corrected 16 Oct 2026 (independent check against the code): lineOverdue compares the committed date (read as midnight) with TODAY, which carries the time of day, so the committed day itself counts as overdue; t2sev is warn from 3 days with no upper end.

items.title: F-043 · Committed date from the lead-time model
items.ask: New order fills the committed date from a lead-time model (July snapshot: 5,000 Kg a day, QC 1 day, dispatch 1 day, raw material 5 days, at least 3 days). Are these the figures you want: A yes, B I will give new figures, C stop filling the date for me?

blocks.p: Committed = received + max(procure days + max(ceil(qty / rate), 1) + QC days + dispatch days, minimum days). Procure days = the slowest raw material not in stock (its lead days, else the default). Rate = the brand's production group rate, else the default rate. ensureMasters fills any missing setting on every load with rate 5,000 Kg/day, QC 1, dispatch 2, RM 7, minimum 3, and once changed an old 8,000 rate to 5,000 (_rate5kV1). leadCfg falls back to 8,000 only when masters.leadTime is missing, which ensureState does not allow.

Worked example: July snapshot masters: rate 5,000, QC 1, dispatch 1, RM 5, minimum 3; Humic group 10,000 a day. A 20,000 Kg Humic line with all RM in stock: 0 + ceil(20,000 / 10,000) = 2 + 1 + 1 = 4 days after received.

blocks.note: Corrected 16 Oct 2026 (independent check against the code): the draft gave 8,000 as the code default; the default actually written is 5,000 (ensureMasters).

items.title: F-044 · Saving: timing and retries

blocks.p: A change is sent 400 ms after the last edit. On a clash (409) the merged copy is saved again up to 5 times straight away, then every 3 seconds until it goes. The 'Now waiting on X' message after a job is checked for 15 minutes after the job was opened.

blocks.p: Worked example: 2 people save within the same second: the second gets 409, merges, and saves again at once.

items.title: F-046 · Go-live dates that switch rules on

blocks.p: Trucks dated on or after 1 Jul 2026 go through the DC control flow (planned, loading, gate pass, release) and FED applies on new POs. Trucks dated on or after 23 Sep 2026 need a passed pre-shipment inspection.
Worked example: a truck dated 20 Sep needs no inspection; one dated 23 Sep does.

items.title: F-047 · DC and gate pass numbers

blocks.p: Next gate pass = GP- and the highest number on any truck or free sample + 1, 4 digits (one book). A free sample's DC is SDC- and its gate pass GP-, 4 digits. A truck gate pass is counted in the person's own copy, so 2 people can take the same number; the clash job asks to renumber one that has not left (LG-22). A free sample's numbers are taken from the higher of this copy and the server's latest copy (smpDispatch), which narrows the gap but does not close it.
Worked example: highest gate pass GP-0141 on a truck and GP-0142 on a sample: the next truck gets GP-0143.

items.title: F-048 · Read and sign: reading time, time to read again, the name match

blocks.p: A part's question shows only when the end of the part has been on screen AND the part has been open for its reading time: 0.3 seconds per word of the part (its lines, picture and what you do now, not the question), at least 5 seconds. After a wrong answer the part is shown again, its answers come in a new order, and the question returns after the end is on screen again and half the reading time has passed, at least 8 seconds.

head: Name
Value
Constant
rows: Time to read again after a wrong answer
half the reading time, at least 8 seconds
About N minutes on the page
all words of the parts for the role, divided by 100, at least 1
Waiting for the server to confirm the sign

blocks.p: The typed name must match the account name after lower-casing, turning every run of characters that are not letters or digits (in any script) into 1 space, and trimming (rsNorm). So 'ali  RAZA.' matches Ali Raza, but 'AliRaza' does not. An account with no name takes any name of 2 or more characters. On a shared login (rsShared: the same logins Back Office calls shared, never the COO) any own name of 3 or more letters is taken.

blocks.note: Worked example: a part of 163 words opens at 09:00:00. Its question cannot show before 09:00:49 (163 x 0.3 = 48.9 seconds), and only once its end has been on screen. A wrong answer at 09:01:10 means the question returns no sooner than 09:01:34 (half of 48.9 is about 24.5 seconds, more than 8).

items.title: F-049 · The month on the bag and its expiry
src: fn bagMonthOf, bagAddMonths, bagShelfMonths, bagShelfFor, packBagFields

blocks.p: Mfg on the bag = the month and year of the packing date. Expiry on the bag = the same month + shelf months. Shelf months: 24 as standard; Production may pick 25 to 36, never shorter; anything outside 24 to 36 is taken as 24. On the 3 correction sheets (Add missing packing, Write the packing record, QC-cleared diverted) the shelf months are those of the latest run of that product and batch number that is not cancelled; 24 if there is none.

Worked example: packed on 16 Oct 2026 with 24 months: Mfg Oct-2026, expiry Oct-2028. With 30 months from 31 Jan 2026: Jan-2026 and Jul-2028. A Night shift that ends on 1 Nov is dated 1 Nov, so its bags are Nov.

blocks.note: The COA is not changed: it keeps the production date and its expiry stays production + 24 months (D-281), so the COA and the bag can show different months.
